title: Ploy
oneLiner: AI-native site builder that uses Jev to pick headline, layout, and copy per visitor segment in milliseconds.
description: Ploy is a marketing site product that personalizes funnel pages without running a full A/B test program for every headline tweak. Builders describe segments and variants; Jev scores which combination fits the incoming visitor context. The public launch clip on X shows roughly twenty-five millisecond decisions per visitor. Listed here as a shipped product pattern for Choice-driven personalization, not a directory stub.

title: rtrvr.ai
oneLiner: Free browser agent that records tasks; Jev speeds routing on the hot path while the LLM still plans steps.
description: rtrvr.ai is a browser automation product aimed at repeatable recorded workflows without forcing every user to bring their own API keys on day one. Community demos highlight Jev shaving latency on routing decisions inside the agent loop while larger models handle open-ended planning. Treat this listing as the product home for the rtrvr.ai domain referenced in builder clips on the showcase.

title: jev-codes
oneLiner: Standards gate for agent-written diffs: YAML rules plus parallel Jev questions before merge.
description: jev-codes is a devtools project from Kushal Agarwal that points Jev at a pull request diff and a YAML standards pack. Instead of one sprawling LLM review essay, the tool asks focused System One questions and surfaces merge-ready opinions. The showcase clip walks through wiring standards once and reusing them across repos.

title: TanStack AI decide()
oneLiner: TanStack AI ships decide() for typed Choice, Score, and boolean paths so agent loops stay structured.
description: TanStack AI is the TanStack team's AI SDK surface. The decide() helper exposes System One style typed decisions to TypeScript apps without hand-rolling HTTP clients for every question schema. Official docs live on tanstack.com; the launch clip on X shows decide() inside real agent code. This listing tracks the integration as a first-class way to call Jev-shaped primitives from TanStack apps.

title: Your Signal
oneLiner: Local feed scoring: Jev ranks posts already on screen against your rules with BYOK and no telemetry pitch.
description: Your Signal is an open experiment from Fabio Angela for ranking social feed items against personal rules on device. The builder clip emphasizes local scoring with bring-your-own-key configuration instead of shipping text to a mystery cloud for relevance labels. Listing tracks the project as described in the public showcase post while we wait for a stable product URL beyond the launch thread.

title: Magic Jev Ball
oneLiner: Playful code-review gate that bounces bad diffs; merge when Jev says yes, not when vibes say maybe.
description: Magic Jev Ball is a builder demo from Agamya that frames code review as a merge gate with visible Jev judgments. The showcase clip treats it as a teaching pattern for parallel questions on diffs before you trust an agent with write access. Primary public reference is the launch post on X until a canonical repo link is published separately.

title: Dub
oneLiner: Link management platform that uses Jev to flag malicious dub.sh URLs trained on historical abuse domains.
description: Dub (dub.co) is a modern link attribution and short-link product used by teams for branded dub.sh links and analytics. Steven Tey's public build clip describes feeding ten thousand plus previously caught malicious domains into Jev so new short links can be scored for abuse before they spread. The approach leans on Jev token efficiency so scanning stays cheap at short-link volume. This listing tracks the shipped abuse-detection pattern from the launch post, not a speculative integration.

title: Avec
oneLiner: Email client that live-prioritizes inbox threads by importance with Jev instead of reverse chronological order.
description: Avec (avec.ai) is an email product from Jonathan Unikowski's team that re-sorts incoming mail by importance as messages arrive. The public showcase clip states the experience is built with Jev and coming to Avec soon, positioning structured ranking as the antidote to endless chronological scrolling. Treat avec.ai as the product home while the app rolls out; Jev usage is described in the attributed launch video on this directory.

title: PixelML
oneLiner: Open-source pixelml-av video indexing with Grok answers and Jev relevance plus support checks on long-form video.
description: PixelML (pixelml.com) builds Composer and Sentinel agents for indexing video to text so LLMs can reason over footage. Sean Phan's benchmark clip compares pixelml-av plus Grok plus Jev against Gemini Flash on a seventy-five minute file: Jev filters retrieved evidence with local temporal context before Grok answers, then runs a support check with optional frame reinspection on low confidence. The pattern targets enterprises with large video corpora and many repeated queries.

title: Hypit
oneLiner: AI UGC creator studio where Jev picks style mixes from your product, audience, and vibe brief.
description: Hypit (hypit.ai) generates distinct AI UGC creators with natural imperfections instead of copy-paste faces. The launch clip claims one hundred unique creators in about thirteen seconds after Jev selects style combinations from a marketer's product, audience, and vibe inputs. Hypit renders the chosen mix into fresh avatars. This listing documents the Choice-driven creative routing pattern from Hypit's attributed post.

title: Egghead Smart AI Procurement
oneLiner: Japanese manufacturing procurement automation combining fast Jev browser ops with ERP systems like SAP and Oracle.
description: Egghead Inc. (egghead.co.jp) sells Smart AI procurement for manufacturers. A public builder clip highlights Jev browser automation speed for tedious ERP data entry into SAP, Oracle, and similar systems, arguing forward-deployed engineering plus Jev beats narrow SaaS alone for shop-floor workflows. The post is in Japanese and focuses on procurement use cases; this listing tracks the product domain and Jev browser routing pattern from the attributed showcase.

title: DocJev
oneLiner: OSS document classify and split library powered by Jev and natural-language category rules, with liteparse or LlamaParse backends.
description: DocJev (github.com/jerryjliu/docjev) is Jerry Liu's open-source library for document classification and splitting using TypeSafe Jev. You provide a document and natural-language category rules; Jev predicts the document category or boundaries between sub-documents. The launch post benchmarks about six times faster than gpt-5.6-luna at equivalent accuracy when using the liteparse OCR path. Optional LlamaParse integration targets complex documents via cloud.llamaindex.ai preprocessing.

title: Jev Social
oneLiner: Local Jev decision loop that drives socai CLI research in the user's Chrome and turns social evidence into cited reports.
description: Jev Social is an open-source, local-first Instagram, TikTok, and LinkedIn research app from socai-io. You describe a goal in plain language; the app builds a bounded set of read-only socai CLI operations discovered from live results (search, open a specific profile or post, read comments, download TikTok media, inspect page state, finish). TypeSafe Jev chooses the next typed operation each step via OpenRouter; socai runs the command in your real Chrome and returns observations. Unsupported, malformed, and low-confidence choices do not execute, and attempted ops drop out of the next choice set. There is no mock fallback, no arbitrary shell generation for Jev, and no handoff to a separate research agent: evidence compiles into cards, tables, and a cited Markdown report. Loopback UI on port 8766, Node 20+, OpenRouter key with Jev access, and the current socai CLI. Live marketing site and GIF demos on GitHub.

title: MFM Search
oneLiner: Search every My First Million upload like a founder with a photographic memory and a very picky research intern.
description: MFM Search is a channel-scoped YouTube demo for @MyFirstMillionPod. You describe a guest, startup idea, or random business rabbit hole; the app understands the query, runs hybrid recall (BM25, TF-IDF, and fuzzy fused with RRF), then fans out multi-question Jev scoring with exists and match gates. Caption enrichment adds jump-to-mention links when transcripts are present. Open source Node and Hono server with a pile UI, mock mode for offline hacking, and a flat-playlist catalog ingest via yt-dlp. Built as a Jev Directory companion demo for the My First Million catalog (~2000+ uploads).
